title: The unbounded tensor pullback and representative coordinates on the existing small model
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X,Y$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use their equivalent small ringed module models and unbounded derived categories [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $a:X\to Y$, conjugate the canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] by the specified module equivalences. This is the additive small-model tensor pullback of [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback], and $La^*$ is its canonical total left derived tensor pullback, with a common localization universe, retaining its derived counit. A flat-term K-flat complex means the existing K-flat predicate [def-pc-kflat-complex] together with flatness of every term [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use the existing total sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the already normalized K-flat derived tensor from the small-model closed tensor-Hom datum; its representative comparison is the one specified by that datum. For $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$, $K'\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\phi:La^*K\to K'$, coordinates consist of a flat-term K-flat complex $P$, a complex $N$, identifications $Q(P)\cong K$ and $Q(N)\cong K'$, invertibility of the derived counit on $P$, and a chain map $a^*P\to N$ whose localized map, composed with the counit and these identifications, is $\phi$. Such coordinates exist without degree bounds. These are universal derived constructions, not arbitrary maps or functors.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Tags 06YS and 07A4; spaces-perfect.tex, equation-bc before Tag 0DKG.

proof.text: For K choose a complex G and the essential-surjectivity identification Q(G) ≅ K. Apply exists_isKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients to G. This gives P → G with K-flat P, flat terms and a quasi-isomorphism. Transport the categorical right-tensor exactness along siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain IsFlatOnSite of each term. Localizing the quasi-isomorphism gives e:Q(P) ≅ K.
Apply the flat-term K-flat counit computation to obtain invertibility of c=(counit g').app P.

Choose a complex N₀ and an identification e₀:Q(N₀) ≅ K'. Apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.left_fac to a=c⁻¹ ≫ Lg'(e.hom) ≫ φ ≫ e₀.inv. It gives a chain map t:g'*(P) → N and s:N₀ → N with Q(s) invertible and a=Q(t) ≫ Q(s)⁻¹. Set e'=Q(s)⁻¹ ≫ e₀. This is the left-fraction lemma as stated in Mathlib, without a K-injective replacement.

Form Coordinates with P,N,t,e,e' and the flatness and counit proofs. Reassociate Q(t) ≫ Q(s)⁻¹ ≫ e₀.hom to a ≫ e₀.hom. Substitute a; cancellation of c with c⁻¹ and e₀.inv with e₀.hom gives precisely c ≫ Q(t) ≫ e'.hom=Lg'(e.hom) ≫ φ.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06YS and flat-term K-flat counit computation in Tag 06YY; coordinate map represented by Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Fractions, DerivedCategory.left_fac.
